entries.headline: Infrastructure damage figures refined: 19 bridges, ~430MW hydropower capacity
entries.body: Nepal Electricity Authority now puts total damaged generation capacity at approximately 430MW (over 12% of Nepal's national hydropower capacity) across the same six facilities reported earlier -- Rasuwagadhi, Chilime, Trishuli 3A, the Trishuli 3B Hub 220kV substation, Trishuli Hydropower Station, and Devighat Hydropower Station -- a modest upward revision from the roughly 405MW/11-project figure in the previous entry. Road-damage reporting now specifies 19 motorable bridges destroyed alongside the ~40km of paved road already noted, and the Pasang Lhamu Highway toward Syabrubesi is confirmed washed away in sections, with restoration work starting only where access currently allows. No confirmed restoration timeline or restart has been reported yet for this event specifically.

entries.headline: Cause investigation reverses a key assumption; rainfall explicitly ruled out
entries.body: Earlier reporting framed the M4.4 earthquake as the likely trigger for the avalanche/landslide that blocked the Lhende Khola. Scientists are now investigating the causality in the other direction too -- whether the avalanche itself was large enough to generate the seismic signal initially attributed to an independent earthquake, rather than the earthquake causing the avalanche. Separately, Nepal's Department of Hydrology and Meteorology has ruled out heavy rainfall in the Rasuwa area on the two days around the event, and authorities say there remains no confirmed evidence of a glacial lake actually bursting (the GLOF hypothesis). Net effect: the cause is less settled than a simple 'earthquake triggered avalanche' narrative implied, not more.

entries.headline: Scale of infrastructure damage detailed; this is the second such event on this river in 14 months
entries.body: A 42km section of the Betrawati (Nuwakot) to Rasuwagadhi road -- the only overland link between Kathmandu and Tibet -- was damaged or washed away, with the Syabrubesi-Rasuwagadhi stretch cut in more than ten places. 11 hydropower projects with a combined 405MW capacity were damaged; the 111MW Rasuwagadhi, Chilime, and Trishuli-3A plants have all halted production. Notably, this is the second time in 14 months this river system has done this: a July 2025 glacial outburst down the Lhende destroyed the same Nepal-China friendship bridge at Rasuwagadhi and killed more than a dozen people -- a recurring risk pattern, not an isolated event.

entries.headline: Casualty figures rise further; sources still disagree on the exact count
entries.body: Nepal Police reportedly put the death toll at 162, while a separate Prime Minister's Office statement cited 95 bodies recovered -- the discrepancy itself hasn't been resolved in reporting. On the Chinese side, missing-person estimates have risen to 550+ (up from 265 previously reported) against 3 confirmed dead. New granularity: 85 Nepali security personnel are among the missing (44 Army, 28 Police, 13 Armed Police Force), plus 60 hydropower workers and 391 foreign + 93 domestic tourists out of contact. All figures remain provisional and inconsistent across sources -- treat any single number cautiously.

entries.headline: Planet adds high-resolution SkySat imagery over Rasuwagadhi and Syabrubesi
entries.body: A new post-event collection appeared in Planet's catalog: 2 SkySat scenes at ~0.8m resolution (vs. 3.8m for the PlanetScope scenes already in this project), acquired 02:00 UTC 27 Aug -- about a day after the flood. Fine enough to resolve individual buildings, bridges, and road sections. Coverage is patchy (50% cloud, ~8% clear fraction) but sharp where visible. Not yet integrated into the web UI's Planet imagery panel (still PlanetScope-only).

entries.headline: Cause still disputed; casualty figures still provisional
entries.body: Planet's own catalog description reports at least 157 deaths in Nepal (Nepal Police) plus 3 deaths and 265 people missing in Gyirong County, Tibet Autonomous Region (Chinese state media) -- all figures explicitly provisional and rising at time of release. Preliminary expert assessment leans toward an ice/rock avalanche from an upper-catchment glacier as the trigger, though a M4.4 earthquake near Gosainkunda and a GLOF from the Puripu Glacier remain live hypotheses pending a detailed investigation.

entries.headline: Planet publishes an open PlanetScope catalog for the event
entries.body: Planet's Crisis Response Program released a dedicated STAC catalog on Source Cooperative: 5 pre-event scenes (27 May 2026, pre-monsoon baseline) and 9 post-event scenes (26 Aug 2026) at 3.8m resolution, CC-BY-NC-4.0. Post-event coverage is 62-93% cloud-obscured -- a concrete illustration of why this project's actual flood-extent detection relies on radar, not optical imagery.

entries.headline: NRSC/ISRO publishes optical confirmation of inundation
entries.body: India's National Remote Sensing Centre published a pre/post comparison (Sentinel-2, 24 Aug vs. Resourcesat-2A AWiFS, 26 Aug) showing visible inundation along the Trishuli River -- independent confirmation outside this project's own Sentinel-1 SAR pipeline.

entries.headline: Copernicus EMS activates EMSR927 for the Bhote Koshi / Trishuli flood
entries.body: The EU's Copernicus Emergency Management Service opened a Rapid Mapping activation for this event, citing a Glacial Lake Outburst Flood (GLOF) as the reported trigger -- one input among several to the still-disputed cause debate. Delivery of the flood-extent/damage products for the Syapru Besi and Timure AOIs was expected 27 Aug 2026, 19:30 UTC.
